rubrics.justification: The response explicitly states no image was provided and relies almost entirely on the Gardner score rather than visual analysis. It also inaccurately describes stage 3 as an expanded blastocyst with thinning zona, which corresponds more to stage 4, so morphology is only partially accurate.
It thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, diagnosis, prior cycle, sperm parameters, endometrium, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis in a clinically meaningful way.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, and the prognosis estimate follows from the favorable factors. Minor issues include overconfidence in some associations and the morphology-stage inconsistency.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice, including SET in a good-prognosis 33-year-old and review of uterine factors after repeated failure. Minor deviations include speculative linkage of TE grade B with aneuploidy and somewhat casual mention of assisted hatching.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support, cycle review, and possible further evaluation if unsuccessful. Some recommendations remain somewhat generic rather than highly case-specific.
